items.text: Sensex fell 121 points to 74,781.76 and Nifty 80 points to 23,398.10, extending India's losing streak to a fifth straight week as crude oil and rising bond yields kept pressure on equities.
Brent crude eased to about $105 a barrel after nearing $110 earlier in the week, but West Asia supply worries kept prices elevated and continued to weigh on oil-import-dependent sectors.
The rupee logged its sharpest weekly fall in four months, slipping to around 95.5-95.6 to the dollar, even as RBI stepped in with dollar sales to slow the decline.
Metal stocks including Vedanta and NALCO fell up to 5% and HDFC Bank hit a fresh 52-week low, while India's 10-year bond yield pushed past 7% on the oil-driven sell-off.
US 10-year Treasury yields climbed near 5% as hot American inflation data firmed up bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike next week, keeping global risk sentiment on edge.
RBI drained roughly Rs 1 lakh crore of surplus banking cash through OMO bond sales in three tranches and failed VRRR auctions, even as it partially trimmed a debt sale as yields spiked.
Governor Malhotra said the RBI has 'nothing off the table' to manage liquidity and the rupee, while flagging balanced inflation risks ahead of the MPC's October policy review.
India's retail inflation is estimated to have risen to a 20-month high of 4.9% in August, narrowing room for a rate cut even as SBI's research arm now expects hikes in October and December.
SEBI and RBI launched a Demat 2.0 pilot letting existing demat accounts hold tokenised corporate bonds without fresh KYC, part of a broader push to widen access to India's bond market.
RBI Governor Malhotra told fintechs to treat customer data as a fiduciary trust, not a business asset, signalling tighter data-governance expectations for lending and payment apps.
US consumer inflation rose 3.4% year-on-year in August, pushing Fed rate-hike bets to around 85-90% for next week's meeting, a reversal from earlier expectations of a cut.
The ECB signalled it may need further rate hikes if energy prices stay elevated, with Bundesbank chief Nagel striking a hawkish tone on the oil-driven inflation shock.
Wall Street rebounded as oil eased, with the Dow up over 500 points, while Asian markets stayed under pressure, with Japan's Nikkei down as much as 3% during the week's crude spike.

Vladimir Putin met Modi in New Delhi ahead of the weekend's BRICS summit, pitching a bloc investment platform, while Modi separately discussed seafarers' safety in West Asia with Iran's president as the oil shock continues.

standfirst: Indian equities closed lower for a fifth straight week as Brent crude near $105 and rising bond yields kept investors cautious, even as RBI moved to drain surplus liquidity and defend the rupee. Hot US inflation data pushed Fed rate-hike bets to near-certain levels for next week, while the ECB struck a similarly hawkish tone on energy-driven price pressures. India hosts BRICS leaders including Vladimir Putin this weekend against this volatile backdrop.
title: Sensex and Nifty extend losing streak to five weeks as oil, Fed rate-hike bets and RBI's cash drain weigh
watch: US Federal Reserve's September 16-17 meeting, where markets now lean toward a rate hike rather than a cut.
BRICS Summit in New Delhi over the weekend, with trade, tariffs and the West Asia oil shock on the agenda.
Whether Brent crude holds below $105 or reignites this week's sell-off in Indian equities and the rupee.
RBI's MPC review in October, with inflation near 5% and yields above 7% narrowing the case for a rate cut.
